name: Genetics acceptance / shave clean

lead: Shaving clean means skipping a sparse or patchy beard and showing a neat, bare face, which gives a tidy look and an unobstructed view of the jaw. Men with limited beard growth, or who simply prefer their face without one, use it as a style decision.

Beard growth starts at puberty, is driven by dihydrotestosterone, and varies partly with genetics. Studies of attractiveness find that preferences for beards depend on context, such as how common beards are and what the rater is looking for, rather than pointing to one best option.

paras: People shave on a regular routine and often pair it with good skincare and a haircut that suits the face shape. Forum threads compare clean-shaven and stubbled photos side by side to help decide. The result is visible right after shaving.

Shaving is low-risk. One forum poster reports it irritates acne-prone skin, and razor nicks or ingrown hairs can happen. In respirator-fit studies clean-shaven faces fit better than bearded ones, though only 47 percent of clean-shaven men achieved adequate fit in one study.

angle.text: Men with limited beard growth, or who prefer their face without one, shave clean to skip a patchy beard and show a neat face with an open view of the jaw. The change is visible straight away. Studies of beard preferences find they depend on context.

lead: Genetics acceptance, or shaving clean, is a looksmaxxing style position that men who cannot grow a full beard, or who look better without one in their own judgment, should shave rather than keep patchy or sparse facial hair. It sits within style metas, discussed on forums such as looksmax.org in threads weighing clean-shaven faces against stubble or beards.

Beard growth begins at puberty, is driven by dihydrotestosterone, and varies partly by genetics.[1] Studies of attractiveness find that preferences for beardedness depend on context, including how common beards are and the rater's mating strategy, rather than pointing to a single best option.[2][3][4][5]
infobox: Shave clean instead of growing a patchy or sparse beard
Beard growth driven by DHT, partly genetic

paras: The practice amounts to accepting limited facial-hair growth and presenting a clean-shaven face. In forum threads users post photos asking whether stubble or a clean shave suits them, and ask what jaw structure is needed to pull off a clean-shaven look.
Dihydrotestosterone, produced from testosterone, stimulates facial hair follicles from puberty, and beard growth rate is partly genetic.[1]

A 2014 study found that the perceived attractiveness of beard thickness depends on how frequent each level is in the surrounding faces, an effect called negative frequency dependence.[2] A 2016 study reported that facial masculinity and beardedness interact in women's ratings of men's attractiveness.[3] Other work found that women's preferences for beardedness vary with relationship context, relationship status, sociosexuality and fecundability.[4][5][6] A study of vocal pitch and facial hair argued that beards may have evolved partly through male-male competition rather than mate attraction.[7]
A study of respirator fit in healthcare workers found that no full-bearded workers achieved an adequate fit and that fit was also adequate in only 47 percent of clean-shaven men.[8]

Fashions have alternated: Romans were largely clean-shaven after Scipio Africanus, shaving was fashionable among 18th-century European elites, beards surged after 1848, and clean-shaven faces dominated 20th-century America before beards returned in the 1960s.[1]
No studies found on genetics acceptance as a practice. Related studies on perceived attractiveness of beards and on respirator fit with facial hair are described above.[2][3][8]
